findings.claim: The job reads `retryCount` into memory and later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` on failure paths. If two cron workers process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same value and overwrite each other's increment, causing lost retry counts and potentially preventing cleanup from ever triggering correctly.
findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increments can lose retries under concurrent cron workers

findings.claim: The initial `deleteMany` uses `OR` with a bare `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch. Because that branch is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, the SMS cron can delete non-SMS workflow reminders solely based on retry count, which is broader than the surrounding SMS-only function.
findings.title: Cleanup deletes reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of reminder method
